findings.title: All functional success criteria map to tasks
findings.description: Cross-referencing the slice's Success Criteria against the task list: protocol conformance (3.1/3.2, 4.1/4.2, 6.2), hand-constructed input correctness (3.2, 4.2), no-neighbor zero force (4.2), stationary-agent zero momentum (3.2), all-zero-neighbor-leadership zero force (4.2), `active_indices` isolation (3.2, 4.2), self-exclusion (4.2), five-force `tick()` directional bias (5.1, 5.2), and profile differentiation (5.3) are each covered. No task traces to nothing (no scope creep): sections 1–2 are prerequisites the slice design itself lists under "Implementation Notes", and section 6 is verification the slice design's Verification Walkthrough calls for. Test tasks immediately follow their implementation tasks (3.1→3.2, 4.1→4.2), and the five commit checkpoints sit at working, tested points rather than after every task.

findings.title: No task updates the server profile bridge, so the full suite cannot go green
findings.description: Task 2.1 makes `leadership_weight` and `momentum_weight` required fields with no defaults, and task 2.2 scopes the fallout update to "search for `BehavioralProfile(` across `tests/`". But production code also constructs it: `build_profiles()` at `src/migratory_server/simulation.py:18` passes exactly the six existing fields, so every construction raises `TypeError` once the new fields land. That breaks `tests/test_simulation.py::TestBuildProfiles` (3 tests), `tests/test_server.py::test_server_runs_with_profiles_config`, and `test_entities_spawned_from_config` (both call `Server.run()`, which calls `build_profiles`). `ProfileConfig` in `src/migratory_server/config.py` also has no fields to carry the new weights, so the fix is not a one-liner the implementer can infer from the plan. The task file never mentions the `src/migratory_server/` package at all. This leaves the requirement "BehavioralProfile ... updates are backward-incompatible by design; all affected tests are updated within this slice" unmet and makes task 6.1 ("All tests pass (existing 80 + new herding tests)") unachievable as written.

findings.title: `leadership` array is not merged by the batch spawn path
findings.description: Task 1.1 extends `AgentState` and updates `create()`, `add_agent()`, and `remove_agent()`, but `EntityManager.spawn_population()` bypasses those helpers: it builds a batch state and then concatenates `positions`, `velocities`, `accelerations`, and `profile_indices` by hand (lines 136–146). With the new array, `state.count` (derived from `positions.shape`) and `state.leadership.shape` desynchronize — the leadership array stays length 0 while the population is non-empty, so any later `LeadershipForce` call in the server path indexes out of bounds. No existing test inspects `leadership` after a batch spawn, so the inconsistency ships silently. No task in the breakdown covers this, and the slice design only says `add_agent()`/`remove_agent()` must handle the array.

findings.title: Vectorization criterion is never stated in any task
findings.description: The slice's Technical Requirements state "Both forces are vectorized within each agent's neighborhood — no nested Python loops." Section 101's task file carried this explicitly for each force ("Use vectorized NumPy within each neighborhood — no `for neighbor in neighbors` inner loop"); sections 3.1 and 4.1 of this file give the per-agent math but never mention vectorization, and the verify steps only check protocol conformance and test results. Task 4.1's `weighted_heading = sum(velocity[i] * leadership[i]) / sum(leadership)` sketch is the shape that invites a per-neighbor Python loop, so a junior implementer could satisfy every written instruction while violating a stated success criterion.

findings.title: Final commit message implies documentation changes no task produces
findings.description: Task 6.3 commits `docs: complete slice 102 — herding and leadership` with "Git add any remaining changes", but no task in the file edits any document — no slice frontmatter/status update, no check-off of the `(102) Herding and Leadership` entry in `100-slices.behavior-engine.md`, no `CHANGELOG.md` entry. Compare slice 303's task file, which has explicit tasks for the slice-design update and CHANGELOG. As written the checkpoint either commits nothing or commits an unspecified change.

findings.title: Commit checkpoints are checkboxes rather than plain marker lines
findings.description: The five commit checkpoints (`1.3`, `2.3`, `3.3`, `4.3`, `5.4`) are written as `- [ ] **1.3 Commit: ...**` checklist items with `- [ ] Git add and commit ...` sub-steps, rather than plain `**Commit**: ...` lines as used in `303-tasks.behavior-engine-integration.md`. Their placement is correct (five markers at working, tested points, not one per task and not only at the end), and CLAUDE.md does mandate checklist formatting for task files, so this is informational only.

No task updates the server profile bridge, so the full suite cannot go green

Vectorization criterion is never stated in any task
Final commit message implies documentation changes no task produces
